model.name: Geometry / Coordinate Reference
model.purpose: Supply the coordinate-reference context that any subject carrying positional data must declare, so that coordinates can be interpreted, compared and operated on without out-of-band assumptions about frame, epoch, axis order or definition provenance.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-033 is a mixin that attaches reference-frame and coordinate-reference context to subjects whose records carry coordinates. It covers how a coordinate reference is identified and resolved, what coordinate system context (axes, units, order) applies, whether the underlying reference frame evolves with time, which epochs are in force and how they differ from record timestamps, which datum realization or ensemble applies, which deformation and vertical/temporal component references apply, how compound references are composed and ordered, and how unknown, custom, engineering-local or superseded definitions are admitted or held as unresolved. It records definitions, references and applicability context. It does not own geometry representation, register maintenance, deformation computation, transformation execution or time-scale realization.
in_scope: Identification of the coordinate reference a position is expressed in, by governed IRI or by register authority, code and register version.
Coordinate system context declared with the reference: axis order, axis direction, axis units and dimensionality.
Reference frame dynamics classification (static, plate-fixed, dynamic) and the frame reference epoch of a dynamic frame.
Coordinate epoch and coordinate metadata binding at a declared scope, and separation of coordinate epoch from observation, transformation, publication and ingestion time.
Datum realization versus datum ensemble resolution, published ensemble accuracy and admissibility for a stated tolerance.
References to deformation and point-motion models with their declared spatial and temporal applicability.
Vertical reference components, their static/dynamic character and the geoid or geopotential realization they cite.
Temporal reference components: temporal datum origin, axis kind and unit, calendar, and the time scale the axis realizes.
Compound reference composition: component references, declared order and the resulting axis sequence.
Unknown, custom, engineering-local, deprecated and superseded definitions, and the sufficiency test that admits or blocks them.
Pinned definition snapshots carrying register version, canonical definition text and an integrity value.
Declared alignments to external coordinate-reference vocabularies and encodings, recorded as alignments rather than conformance claims.
out_of_scope: Geometry representation itself: primitives, topology, validity rules, tessellation, generalization and spatial indexing, which belong to the parent geometry model WM-XCT-010.

Maintenance of external registers such as the EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset, OGC Naming Authority definitions and national registers; entry creation, revision, deprecation and publication remain with those authorities.
Computation, fitting or distribution of deformation models, velocity grids, geoid models and post-seismic deformation parameters.
Execution of coordinate conversions, transformations and point-motion operations, operation selection, pipeline construction and operation-accuracy assessment.
Realization of time scales, maintenance of leap-second tables and calendar arithmetic.
Positional accuracy and uncertainty budgets beyond recording published ensemble accuracy and declared model extents.
Storage formats and access interfaces (WKT text, PROJJSON, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, Git, MCP, MongoDB), which are projections of this context rather than its semantics.
Audit trails for transformation execution, deformation evaluation or downstream use of coordinates.

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent owns what a geometry is (primitives, topology, extent, validity). This entry owns what the geometry's coordinates are referenced to. ISO 19111 / OGC Topic 2 keep the coordinate set and the coordinate reference system as separate concepts, so a coordinate tuple only becomes an interpretable geometry when both are present.

ISO 19111 separates a CRS definition from a coordinate operation, including the point motion operation that moves coordinates between epochs within one dynamic CRS. This entry records the transformation reference epoch and the citation of an operation; selecting, parameterizing, executing and accuracy-assessing operations belongs to the operation model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset and other definition registers
boundary_notes.distinction: Registers are the authoritative master systems for definitions and carry their own versioning, deprecation and data-management policies. This entry carries authority, code, register version, canonical snapshot and digest, and must never become a second register or re-publish register content wholesale.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Deformation model publication (OGC Topic 24 functional model and national agency products)
boundary_notes.distinction: A deformation model is a published product with its own element decomposition, spatial and time functions, versions and extents. This entry cites it and records applicability limits; it never evaluates spatial or time functions, interpolates grids or computes displacement.

BIPM produces UTC and TAI and the CGPM decides leap-second policy, while IERS monitors UT1. This entry records which time scale a temporal axis realizes and the temporal datum origin; it does not realize, steer or convert time scales, nor maintain leap-second tables.

Published datum ensemble accuracy and declared model extents are recorded here as reference context. Survey accuracy, error propagation, uncertainty budgets and fitness-for-purpose assessment belong to a measurement model.

WKT-CRS text, PROJJSON, GeoPackage srs tables and GeoTIFF keys are carriers of this context, not its semantics. Where a carrier cannot hold required context (for example GeoJSON, which fixes WGS 84 and removed the crs member), the inability is recorded as a conflict and a degradation decision, never as a change of meaning.

sources.title: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 2: Referencing by coordinates Corrigendum
sources.version_or_date: OGC 18-005r5, version 5.0.1, published 2021-07-02 (consistent with ISO 19111:2019 and its Amendment 1:2021)
sources.relevance: Normative source for dynamic reference frame (3.1.20), frame reference epoch (3.1.29), coordinate epoch (3.1.7), coordinate set defined as tuples sharing one CRS and, if dynamic, one coordinate epoch, datum ensemble (3.1.16), point motion operation (3.1.48), compound CRS (3.1.3), temporal CRS/datum (3.1.63-3.1.65), vertical CRS/reference frame (3.1.70-3.1.72), engineering CRS/datum (3.1.25-3.1.26) and the conformance classes for relating coordinates to coordinate metadata.

sources.title: ISO 19111:2019 Geographic information — Referencing by coordinates
sources.version_or_date: Third edition 2019-01, with Amendment 1:2021 and Amendment 2:2023; revision under ISO/AWI 19111
sources.relevance: The conceptual schema and minimum data required to describe coordinate reference systems and coordinate operations; states that a CRS definition does not change with time although defining parameters may include rates of change, and that metadata for a dataset referenced to a dynamic CRS should include coordinate epoch information.

sources.title: Geographic information — Well-known text representation of coordinate reference systems (OGC 18-010r7 / ISO 19162:2019)
sources.version_or_date: OGC 18-010r7, version 2.0.6, published 2019-08-13; superseded for new work by 18-010r11 (WKT-CRS 2.1, 2023)
sources.relevance: Canonical text encoding of CRS definitions: DYNAMIC and FRAMEEPOCH (clause 7.6), ENSEMBLE and ENSEMBLEACCURACY, COORDINATEMETADATA with EPOCH/COORDEPOCH (clause 16), COMPOUNDCRS component ordering (clause 15), TIMECRS/TDATUM/TIMEORIGIN/TIMEUNIT/CALENDAR (clause 13), VERTCRS/VDATUM (clause 10), ENGCRS/EDATUM (clause 11) and the ID element with authority, code, version, citation and URI (clause 7.3.3).

sources.title: OGC Abstract Specification Topic 24: Functional Model for Crustal Deformation
sources.organization: Open Geospatial Consortium (with IAG Commission 1 Working Group 1.3.1)
sources.relevance: Defines a deformation model as displacement of the Earth's surface within a defined spatial and temporal extent (clause 1), decomposed into elements each having a spatial function and a time function (clauses 5.2-5.4), with model extents beyond which the model is undefined (5.1), model and element attributes including uncertainty (5.5-5.6), and application to coordinate operations including epoch-to-epoch deformation (clause 6). Establishes that deformation evaluation is an operation, distinct from recording a reference.

sources.title: OGC API - Features - Part 2: Coordinate Reference Systems by Reference corrigendum
sources.relevance: Requirement 1 mandates CRS referenceability by URI in the form http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/{authority}/{version}/{code}; defines default CRS84 and CRS84h; Recommendation 2 states that for a dynamic storage CRS the storageCrsCoordinateEpoch property should give the coordinate epoch as a decimal year, and states that coordinates referenced to a dynamic CRS are ambiguous if the coordinate epoch is unknown.

sources.title: ITRF2020 — International Terrestrial Reference Frame
sources.organization: IERS ITRS Centre, Institut national de l'information géographique et forestière (IGN)
sources.version_or_date: ITRF2020, released 2023, reference epoch 2015.0 (Altamimi et al., Journal of Geodesy, 2023)
sources.relevance: Authoritative example of a dynamic reference frame realization: station positions and velocities defined at a stated reference epoch, post-seismic deformation models applied for stations affected by major earthquakes, and published transformation parameters between successive realizations. Grounds the distinction between a realization, its frame reference epoch and a user's coordinate epoch.

sources.title: New Datums — NSRS Modernization
sources.relevance: National authority replacing NAD 83 with four plate-fixed dynamic terrestrial reference frames (NATRF2022, PATRF2022, CATRF2022, MATRF2022) each defined relative to ITRF2020 and rotating with a tectonic plate, plus a gravity-based geopotential datum realized through a geoid model. Evidence that frame dynamics classification and vertical realization references must be explicit and regionally varied.

sources.title: New Zealand Geodetic Datum 2000 deformation model
sources.version_or_date: Deformation model version 20180701; page last updated 2020-01-13; seven released versions since 20130801
sources.relevance: Semi-dynamic datum practice: NZGD2000 aligned to ITRF96 at epoch 2000.0, with a versioned deformation model comprising a secular velocity component and earthquake patches. States that model versions are named by approximate publication date, a naming convention that must not be confused with an identifier or a coordinate epoch.

sources.title: Geomatics Guidance Note 25 — Dynamic versus static CRSs and use of the ITRF (IOGP Report 373-25)
sources.organization: International Association of Oil & Gas Producers (IOGP) Geomatics Committee
sources.relevance: Recommended practice for the use of dynamic CRSs and their relationship to static CRSs, treating ITRF and WGS 84 as dynamic references and addressing coordinate epoch recording. Explicitly scoped as practical guidance rather than a comprehensive normative treatment, which is why it is used to corroborate rather than to found structure.

sources.title: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset — Guidance Notes and Registry
sources.version_or_date: EPSG Dataset v13.001 / GeoRepository v2.44.2; GN 7-1 v9 (Mar 2025), GN 7-2 v74 (Jul 2026), GN 7-3 v1.0 (Jul 2022), GN 7-6 Policies and procedures for data management v1.1 (Jun 2025), GN 7-7 ETRS89 in the EPSG Dataset v1 (Apr 2026); accessed 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: The authoritative register for CRS, datum and coordinate operation definitions, with explicit dataset versioning, documented data-management policies and a deprecation mechanism for invalid items. Grounds the requirement to pin register authority, code and register version rather than to cite a bare code.

sources.title: RFC 7946: The GeoJSON Format
sources.relevance: Counterexample and interoperability floor: fixes all coordinates to a WGS 84 geographic CRS in decimal degrees, and Appendix B records that the 2008 crs member was removed entirely, with alternative CRSs permitted only by prior arrangement outside the specification. Demonstrates that some carriers cannot convey a CRS reference or a coordinate epoch at all.

sources.title: OGC GeoPackage Encoding Standard 1.4.0
sources.relevance: Concrete evidence of non-register and dynamic CRS handling in a carrier: gpkg_spatial_ref_sys requires rows with srs_id -1 (undefined cartesian) and 0 (undefined geographic) alongside a WKT definition column (Requirement 10), with a definition_12_063 extension column for ISO 19162:2019 WKT and an epoch extension column for dynamic CRSs.

sources.title: PROJJSON specification
sources.version_or_date: PROJJSON schema v0.7 (https://proj.org/schemas/v0.7/projjson.schema.json), introduced in PROJ 9.2.1; documentation for PROJ 9.8.x
sources.relevance: A JSON encoding of WKT2:2019 / ISO 19162:2019 with declared support for CoordinateMetadata (v0.6+), coordinate epoch, datum ensemble, deformation_models (v0.5+), compound CRS, temporal CRS and datum, engineering CRS, and id/ids members. Demonstrates a format-neutral canonical form for pinned definition snapshots.

sources.title: Coordinate epoch support
sources.version_or_date: GDAL 3.4 and later; stable documentation accessed 2026-09-04
sources.relevance: Implementation evidence on epoch binding scope: epoch is stored as a property of the CRS at dataset or layer level because almost no format allows per-observation epoch storage; carriers include the WKT:2019 EPOCH subnode in FlatGeobuf, the epoch column in gpkg_spatial_ref_sys, CoordinateEpochGeoKey 5120 in GeoTIFF, and coordinateEpoch attributes in .aux.xml and VRT. Epoch is expressed as a decimal year.

sources.title: Resolution 4 of the 27th CGPM (2022) — On the use and future development of UTC
sources.organization: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures (BIPM) / Conférence Générale des Poids et Mesures
sources.version_or_date: 27th CGPM, November 2022; implementation plan due for the 28th CGPM (2026)
sources.relevance: Authoritative statement that UTC is produced by BIPM at the same rate as TAI differing by an integral number of seconds, that leap seconds are applied when IERS predicts UT1-UTC approaching 0.9 s, and that the maximum UT1-UTC difference will be increased in or before 2035. Grounds the requirement to record which time scale a temporal axis realizes and to treat leap-second behaviour as a declared constraint.

bundles.name: Time-Dependent Reference Frame Context
bundles.description: Context establishing whether a coordinate reference evolves with time, which frame realization or ensemble applies, which epochs are in force, and which deformation model reference governs movement between epochs.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19111 and OGC Topic 2 make dynamic reference frames, frame reference epoch and coordinate epoch first-class concepts, and OGC API - Features Part 2 states plainly that coordinates referenced to a dynamic CRS are ambiguous if the coordinate epoch is unknown. An agent therefore cannot interpret, compare or operate on positional data without this bundle, and the epochs involved are routinely confused with record timestamps.

layers.name: Reference Frame Dynamics and Epoch Declaration
layers.description: Whether the underlying reference frame is static, plate-fixed or dynamic, the frame reference epoch that defines a dynamic frame, the coordinate epoch attached to coordinate values, and the strict separation of these geodetic instants from record time.

findings.name: Reference frame dynamics classification
findings.description: Declares explicitly whether the reference frame underlying a coordinate reference is static, plate-fixed or dynamic in the ISO 19111 sense that its defining parameters include time evolution, and records the frame reference epoch when the frame is dynamic. Frame dynamics is never inferred from a CRS name or code.

questions.text: Is the underlying reference frame static, plate-fixed or dynamic, and which defining clause or register attribute establishes that?
answer_data: frame dynamics classification code
citing clause, register attribute or WKT DYNAMIC element that establishes it
name of the declaring authority

questions.text: What frame reference epoch defines this dynamic reference frame, and in which notation is it expressed?
answer_data: frame reference epoch as a decimal year in the Gregorian calendar
equivalent RFC 3339 instant with seconds and explicit offset
statement of which notation is authoritative for geodetic arithmetic

questions.text: Which authority defines and publishes this frame realization, under which document and at which version?
answer_data: defining authority name
defining document identifier and version
publication date of the realization

questions.text: What evidence justifies treating the frame as static for the subject's stated positional tolerance?
answer_data: stated positional tolerance with unit
expected intra-frame velocity or displacement magnitude over the data lifetime
justification note with approving role and decision reference

data_elements.name: Frame dynamics code
data_elements.description: Controlled value declaring the frame as static, plate-fixed dynamic, or globally dynamic, per the ISO 19111 dynamic reference frame concept.

data_elements.name: Frame reference epoch
data_elements.description: The epoch of the coordinates that define a dynamic reference frame, stored as a decimal year with an equivalent RFC 3339 instant. Present only when the frame is dynamic; it is a property of the frame definition, not of any record.

data_elements.name: Frame defining authority reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the authority and document that define the frame realization, with the document version.

data_elements.name: Static treatment decision
data_elements.description: Recorded decision, with tolerance and approver, to treat a frame as static for a stated purpose despite known time evolution.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding is purely declarative reference data read from the frame's own defining publication or register entry. It produces no document of its own: the authoritative artefact is the realization publication owned by the geodetic authority, and creating a local artefact here would imply that this model publishes or maintains frame realizations, which the boundary notes exclude.

findings.name: Coordinate epoch and coordinate metadata binding
findings.description: Binds a coordinate set to its coordinate reference and, when that reference is dynamic, to the coordinate epoch, at an explicitly declared binding scope. Records the carrier that conveys the epoch and the disposition when no epoch is available.

questions.text: Is a coordinate epoch required for this coordinate set, and which rule or policy makes it required?
answer_data: epoch requirement flag
citation of the requiring clause, recommendation or adopting-Dimension policy
distinction between normative recommendation and local policy obligation

questions.text: At which scope is the coordinate epoch bound — dataset, layer, feature or individual coordinate tuple?
answer_data: binding scope code
identifier of the bound coordinate set at that scope
note on whether the carrier can preserve the scope on round trip

questions.text: Which coordinate epoch value applies to these coordinates, in decimal year and as an RFC 3339 instant?
answer_data: coordinate epoch as decimal year
equivalent RFC 3339 instant with seconds and explicit offset
source of the epoch value (survey record, producer declaration or register default)

questions.text: What disposition is recorded when a dynamic reference is used but no coordinate epoch can be established?
answer_data: unresolved-epoch state code
prohibited uses while unresolved
escalation target and reason text

questions.text: Which carrier field conveys the coordinate epoch in the chosen encoding, and what is lost if the carrier is absent?
answer_data: carrier field identifier such as a WKT EPOCH subnode, an srs table epoch column or a format-specific epoch key
loss statement when the carrier cannot hold the epoch
declared degradation or rejection decision

data_elements.name: Coordinate epoch
data_elements.description: The epoch to which coordinates in a dynamic coordinate reference system are referenced, as a decimal year with an RFC 3339 equivalent. It is not the time the record was created, observed or ingested.

data_elements.name: Epoch binding scope
data_elements.description: Controlled value stating whether the coordinate epoch is bound at dataset, layer, feature or coordinate-tuple level.

data_elements.name: Coordinate reference identifier
data_elements.description: Governed IRI, or register authority plus code plus register version, identifying the coordinate reference the coordinate set is expressed in.

data_elements.name: Epoch absence disposition
data_elements.description: State recorded when a dynamic reference lacks a coordinate epoch, together with the uses it blocks.

artifacts.name: Coordinate metadata record
artifacts.description: A record binding one coordinate set to its coordinate reference and, where the reference is dynamic, to its coordinate epoch and binding scope, corresponding to the ISO 19111 coordinate metadata concept and the WKT COORDINATEMETADATA construct.
media_or_form: carrier-native epoch field such as a spatial reference table epoch column or a coordinate epoch key
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified first by the authoritative master-system identifier of the coordinate set it annotates; failing that by the governed CRS IRI combined with the declared coordinate epoch and binding scope; failing that by a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Neither the coordinate epoch nor any date is used as the identifier.

findings.name: Separation of epoch and record time semantics
findings.description: Keeps coordinate epoch, observation time, transformation reference epoch, definition publication time and ingestion time as distinct recorded roles, so that a geodetic reference instant is never read as a record timestamp and a record timestamp is never substituted for an epoch.

questions.text: Which distinct time roles are recorded for this coordinate set, and how is each one defined?
answer_data: enumerated time roles in use
definition text and citing clause per role
statement of which roles are mandatory for the subject

questions.text: Does the observation time of these coordinates differ from their coordinate epoch, and what reconciled them?
answer_data: observation time as an RFC 3339 instant with offset
coordinate epoch as decimal year
citation of the operation or model applied to reconcile them, without its execution details

questions.text: When was the cited reference or deformation-model definition published, and when was this record ingested?
answer_data: definition publication date of the cited authority document or register release
ingestion timestamp in RFC 3339 with offset
identity of the ingesting agent or process

questions.text: Which validation prevents a coordinate epoch from being stored or interpreted as a record creation timestamp?
answer_data: validation rule identifier and description
failure mode it blocks
action taken on failure

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: The instant at which the position was observed or surveyed, in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset. Distinct from the coordinate epoch the coordinates are expressed at.

data_elements.name: Transformation reference epoch
data_elements.description: The epoch a cited coordinate operation or point motion operation is parameterized against, recorded as a citation-side attribute only.

data_elements.name: Definition publication time
data_elements.description: Publication date of the cited reference definition, register release or deformation-model version, as declared by its publishing authority.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: The instant this model's record was created or last refreshed from its source, in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Time role map
data_elements.description: Explicit mapping from each recorded time value to its declared semantic role, preventing silent reuse of one value for another role.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The content here is a set of discrete typed time values plus their role mapping, all carried inline on the record they qualify. Emitting a separate artefact would create a second place where the same instants live and would reintroduce exactly the conflation the finding exists to prevent, so this context is deliberately inline and reference-only.

layers.name: Datum Realization and Deformation Model References
layers.description: Whether a coordinate reference resolves to a specific datum realization or to a datum ensemble, and which published deformation or point-motion model reference a consumer must apply to move between epochs.

findings.name: Datum ensemble versus specific realization
findings.description: Records whether the reference resolves to a datum ensemble of multiple realizations treated as not significantly different, or to one named realization member, together with the published ensemble accuracy and the admissibility decision for the subject's tolerance.

questions.text: Does this coordinate reference resolve to a datum ensemble or to a single named realization member?
answer_data: resolution kind code
ensemble identifier where applicable
member realization identifier where determinable

questions.text: What ensemble accuracy is published for this ensemble, and does it satisfy the subject's positional tolerance?
answer_data: published ensemble accuracy value with unit
subject positional tolerance with unit
comparison outcome and approving role

questions.text: Which realization members belong to the ensemble, and which member actually produced these coordinates?
answer_data: list of member realization references
producing member reference or explicit undetermined state
evidence supporting the producing-member attribution

questions.text: Under which constraint is ensemble-level referencing prohibited for this subject?
answer_data: constraint statement and its source
tolerance threshold that triggers it
required substitute action, such as citing a specific member

data_elements.name: Datum ensemble reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the datum ensemble a coordinate reference resolves to, where ensemble-level referencing is used.

data_elements.name: Realization member reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the specific datum realization that produced or governs the coordinates.

data_elements.name: Published ensemble accuracy
data_elements.description: The ensemble accuracy declared by the defining authority, as a quantity with unit, copied as reference context and not recomputed.

data_elements.name: Ensemble admissibility decision
data_elements.description: Recorded decision on whether ensemble-level referencing is admissible for the subject, with tolerance and approver.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Ensemble composition, member list and published ensemble accuracy are register-owned facts resolved against the defining authority. This model carries only the resolution outcome and the local admissibility decision as inline reference data; materialising a local ensemble document would duplicate register content that the boundary notes assign to the register authority.

findings.name: Deformation and point-motion model reference
findings.description: Cites the deformation or point-motion model a consumer must apply to propagate coordinates between epochs, with identifier, publisher, version and declared spatial and temporal extent, and records what happens outside that extent. No displacement is computed, interpolated or stored here.

questions.text: Which deformation or point-motion model, at which published version, governs epoch propagation for this reference?
answer_data: deformation model identifier
published version label as issued by the publisher
resolvable location of the published model

questions.text: What spatial and temporal extent bounds the cited deformation model's declared validity?
answer_data: spatial extent as a bounding geometry or named region with its own CRS reference
temporal validity interval with RFC 3339 bounds
statement that the model is undefined outside these bounds

questions.text: Which authority publishes, versions and evaluates the cited deformation model?
answer_data: publishing authority name
statement that evaluation and grid distribution are owned externally
reference to the model that owns operation execution

questions.text: What is recorded when the subject location or required epoch falls outside the cited model's declared extent?
answer_data: out-of-extent state code
prohibited uses while out of extent
alternative model reference or explicit gap record

data_elements.name: Deformation model reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable citation of the deformation or point-motion model that governs epoch propagation, carried as a reference only.

data_elements.name: Deformation model version label
data_elements.description: The publisher's version label for the cited model, recorded verbatim even where the publisher names versions by approximate publication date; the label is not treated as a date value or an identifier of this record.

data_elements.name: Deformation applicability extent
data_elements.description: The spatial extent within which the cited model is declared valid, expressed with its own coordinate reference.

data_elements.name: Out-of-extent disposition
data_elements.description: State and prohibited-use statement recorded when the subject falls outside the cited model's spatial or temporal extent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The deformation model itself, its element decomposition, its grids and its evaluation are published, versioned and executed by the geodetic authority that owns it. This model records only a resolvable citation, a version pin and an applicability note, all of which are reference values on the record. Declaring a local artefact would imply custody of the grid or of the displacement computation, which the composition links assign to the deformation-model publisher and to the coordinate-operation model.

bundles.name: Composite, Temporal and Non-Register Definition Context
bundles.description: Context for references that are not a single current horizontal register entry: temporal and vertical components, compound composition and ordering, and definitions that are unknown, custom, engineering-local, superseded or preserved as governed snapshots.
bundles.rationale: ISO 19111 and WKT-CRS admit compound, temporal, vertical and engineering references as first-class constructs, registers version and deprecate entries, and carriers such as GeoPackage explicitly provide undefined cartesian and undefined geographic rows. Positional data therefore routinely arrives with references that a bare code cannot resolve, and an agent needs an explicit sufficiency test and a pinning mechanism rather than a silent default.

layers.name: Temporal and Vertical Reference Components
layers.description: The non-horizontal components a position may be referenced against: a temporal axis with its datum origin, unit, calendar and time scale, and a vertical frame with its dynamics and geopotential realization.

findings.name: Temporal reference, datum origin and time scale
findings.description: Records the temporal datum origin, the temporal axis kind and unit, the calendar in use, and the time scale the axis realizes, together with the leap-second exposure that follows from choosing a rotation-linked scale.

questions.text: What is the temporal datum origin of this axis, and in which calendar is it expressed?
answer_data: temporal datum origin as an RFC 3339 instant with offset
calendar identifier
citing definition clause or register entry

questions.text: Which time scale does the temporal axis realize, and which authority maintains that scale?
answer_data: time scale identifier such as an atomic, coordinated or navigation-system scale
maintaining authority name
reference to the authority's defining resolution or bulletin

questions.text: Is the temporal axis a date-time, a temporal count or a temporal measure, and what unit does it use?
answer_data: temporal axis kind code
axis unit identifier and conversion factor where applicable
axis direction and range meaning where declared

questions.text: How are leap seconds and the decided future change to the maximum UT1-UTC difference handled on this axis?
answer_data: leap-second handling statement for the chosen scale
affected comparison or arithmetic operations
review trigger tied to the announced change and its owning authority

data_elements.name: Temporal datum origin
data_elements.description: The origin instant of the temporal datum, in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset, with the calendar named separately.

data_elements.name: Time scale code
data_elements.description: Controlled value naming the time scale the temporal axis realizes, together with its maintaining authority.

data_elements.name: Temporal axis kind
data_elements.description: Controlled value distinguishing a date-time axis, a temporal count axis and a temporal measure axis.

data_elements.name: Temporal axis unit
data_elements.description: Unit of the temporal axis with its conversion factor where the unit is not a base unit.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are a small set of declared parameters that qualify a temporal axis and are always read together with the reference definition they belong to. The authoritative documents are the time-scale authority's resolutions and the CRS definition itself, both external; a local artefact would either duplicate the pinned definition snapshot or imply that this model realizes a time scale, which the boundary notes exclude.

findings.name: Vertical reference component and its dynamics
findings.description: Records the vertical reference frame heights or depths refer to, whether that frame is static or dynamic with its own frame reference epoch, the axis direction and unit, and the geoid or geopotential model version through which the frame is realized.
