answer_data: vertical reference frame identifier with register authority and version
frame name as published
extent over which the frame is declared valid

questions.text: Is the vertical reference frame static or dynamic, and does it carry its own frame reference epoch distinct from the horizontal frame?
answer_data: vertical frame dynamics code
vertical frame reference epoch where dynamic
statement of whether it differs from the horizontal frame epoch

questions.text: Through which geoid or geopotential model version is the vertical frame realized?
answer_data: geoid or geopotential model identifier and version
publishing authority
publication date of that model version

questions.text: Is the vertical axis a height with up positive or a depth with down positive, and in what unit?
answer_data: axis direction code
axis unit identifier
note on sounding or hydrographic sign conventions where they apply

data_elements.name: Vertical reference frame identifier
data_elements.description: Governed identifier of the vertical reference frame that heights or depths are referenced to.

data_elements.name: Vertical frame dynamics code
data_elements.description: Controlled value declaring the vertical frame as static or dynamic, tracked separately from horizontal frame dynamics.

data_elements.name: Geoid or geopotential model reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the geoid or geopotential model version realizing the vertical frame, carried as a citation only.

data_elements.name: Vertical axis direction
data_elements.description: Controlled value stating whether the axis increases upward as a height or downward as a depth, with its unit.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The vertical component is a set of declared attributes resolved against the register entry and the geoid model publication, both externally owned. Where a definition text is needed it is captured once by the pinned definition snapshot artefact rather than duplicated here, so this finding holds inline reference data only.

layers.name: Compound Reference Composition
layers.description: How independent component references are combined into one compound coordinate reference, in what declared order, and what axis sequence and epoch applicability result.

findings.name: Compound reference components and ordering
findings.description: Enumerates the component references of a compound coordinate reference, their declared sequence, the resulting axis order and units, the independence condition that admits the combination, and how a coordinate epoch scopes across components.

questions.text: Which component coordinate references make up this compound reference?
answer_data: ordered list of component reference identifiers
component kind per entry, such as horizontal, vertical, temporal or parametric
register authority and version per component

questions.text: In which order are the components declared, and what axis sequence and units result from that order?
answer_data: component sequence indices
resulting ordered axis list with direction and unit per axis
statement that axis order is recorded explicitly and never inferred from a code

questions.text: What evidence shows the components are independent, as a compound reference requires?
answer_data: independence assessment outcome
reason text citing the definition of independence between component references
assessing role and decision reference

questions.text: If any component is dynamic, does the coordinate epoch apply to that component alone or to the whole compound reference?
answer_data: epoch applicability scope code
identifier of the component the epoch qualifies
note on how the carrier expresses that scope

questions.text: How is the compound reference degraded or rejected when a consumer supports only one component?
answer_data: degradation decision such as reject, project to a named component, or hold
component retained and components dropped
warning text propagated to the consumer

data_elements.name: Component reference list
data_elements.description: Ordered collection of the component coordinate reference identifiers that constitute the compound reference.

data_elements.name: Component sequence index
data_elements.description: Explicit position of each component in the declared compound order, used as the canonical ordering key.

data_elements.name: Resulting axis order
data_elements.description: The ordered axis list produced by the compound composition, each axis carrying name, direction and unit.

data_elements.name: Epoch applicability scope
data_elements.description: Controlled value stating whether a coordinate epoch qualifies one named component or the whole compound reference.

artifacts.name: Compound reference composition record
artifacts.description: A record listing the component references of a compound coordinate reference with their declared sequence, the resulting axis order with directions and units, the independence assessment outcome and the epoch applicability scope.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified first by the register authority's own code and register version where the compound reference is a register entry; otherwise by a governed IRI constructed from the ordered component identifiers; otherwise by a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. No date or epoch is used as the identifier.

layers.name: Non-Register, Custom and Pinned Definitions
layers.description: References that are not resolvable as a current register entry — unknown, custom, engineering-local, deprecated or superseded — and the governed snapshots that keep historic coordinates interpretable.

findings.name: Unknown, custom and engineering definition sufficiency
findings.description: Tests whether a non-register reference carries a resolvable definition or a complete governed snapshot sufficient to interpret coordinates without external lookup. A bare local name or a numeric code alone is insufficient and produces an unresolved state that blocks positional use.

questions.text: Is this reference unknown, custom, engineering-local, or a deprecated or superseded register entry?
answer_data: non-register kind code
evidence for the classification such as an undefined srs row, a missing register match or a deprecation flag
originating system or producer

questions.text: Does this reference carry a resolvable definition or a complete governed snapshot sufficient to interpret coordinates without external lookup?
answer_data: sufficiency outcome code
list of missing defining elements where insufficient, such as datum, ellipsoid, prime meridian, axes, units or anchor
rule citation stating that a bare local name or numeric code is insufficient

questions.text: For an engineering or local reference, which anchor point, orientation and carrier object define it, and does that carrier move?
answer_data: anchor point description with its own coordinate reference where known
axis orientation definition
carrier object identity and whether it is fixed or moving, with the moving-carrier consequence for epoch semantics

questions.text: Which state is recorded when a definition cannot be resolved, and which uses are then prohibited?
answer_data: unresolved state code
prohibited operations while unresolved, such as merging, reprojection or distance computation
review owner and re-evaluation trigger

questions.text: Who may register, amend or approve a custom definition for the adopting Dimension?
answer_data: authorized role names
approval record reference
restriction note where the definition discloses a sensitive site anchor

data_elements.name: Definition sufficiency state
data_elements.description: Controlled value recording whether the reference is fully resolvable, sufficient by governed snapshot, or unresolved and blocking.

data_elements.name: Local definition payload
data_elements.description: The complete definition text supplied with a non-register reference, in a canonical encoding, when no register entry resolves it.

data_elements.name: Engineering anchor description
data_elements.description: Anchor point, axis orientation and carrier object for an engineering or local reference, including whether the carrier is fixed or moving.

data_elements.name: Definition resolution identifier
data_elements.description: Governed IRI or register locator at which the definition can be resolved, absent for purely local definitions.

artifacts.name: Custom reference definition package
artifacts.description: A self-contained definition for a non-register coordinate reference, complete enough to interpret coordinates without external lookup: datum or anchor, ellipsoid or carrier description, axis names, directions and units, and any conversion parameters.
media_or_form: WKT-CRS text carrying the full definition
format-neutral parameter set with anchor and axis descriptions
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified first by the originating master system's own identifier for the local reference where one exists; otherwise by a governed IRI minted in the adopting Dimension's namespace, which must not shadow any register code; otherwise by a UUID or ULID. A site name, project name or date is never used as the identifier.

findings.name: Pinned definition snapshot and register provenance
findings.description: Preserves the exact canonical definition text, register authority, code and register version in force when coordinates were produced, with an integrity value, so that later register revisions, deprecations or supersessions do not silently change how historic coordinates are interpreted.

questions.text: Which register authority, register version and code identify the definition in force for these coordinates?
answer_data: register authority code
register version or dataset release identifier
definition code within that register, plus the governed IRI form where available

questions.text: Which canonical form and integrity value fix the pinned definition text against silent drift?
answer_data: canonical form identifier, such as normalized WKT-CRS text or a named JSON schema version
digest algorithm and digest value
verification outcome and last verification timestamp

questions.text: How is a pinned snapshot marked when the register later deprecates or supersedes the entry?
answer_data: supersession state code
superseding entry reference where the register names one
observation timestamp of the upstream change, recorded separately from the register's own publication date

questions.text: How long must a pinned snapshot be retained relative to the coordinates that cite it, and who executes disposal?
answer_data: retention rule tied to the life of the citing coordinate sets
tombstone content preserved after disposal
reference to the policy and master system that own disposal execution

data_elements.name: Register authority code
data_elements.description: Controlled value naming the register authority that issued the definition, such as a geodetic parameter register or a naming authority.

data_elements.name: Register version
data_elements.description: The register release or dataset version in force when the definition was pinned, recorded verbatim as the authority publishes it.

data_elements.name: Definition code
data_elements.description: The authority's own code for the definition, used as the primary identifier component together with the register authority and version.

data_elements.name: Definition snapshot digest
data_elements.description: Digest computed over the canonical definition text plus register authority, version and code, used to detect drift or corruption.

data_elements.name: Supersession state
data_elements.description: Controlled value recording whether the pinned entry remains current, has been deprecated upstream, or has been superseded, with the superseding reference.

artifacts.name: Pinned reference definition snapshot
artifacts.description: An immutable capture of one coordinate reference definition as it stood at a named register version, holding the canonical definition text, the register authority, version and code, the digest and the supersession state. Successive captures of the same definition across register versions form a sequence.
media_or_form: register export record in a format-neutral structured form
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified first by the register authority's code together with the register version, which is the authoritative master-system identifier for the definition; otherwise by the governed CRS IRI including its version segment; otherwise by a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Snapshot sequence position is a separate serial number and never a date, even where the upstream publisher names releases by date.

functions.name: Declare coordinate reference binding
functions.description: Attach a resolvable coordinate reference to a subject's coordinate set and, where the underlying frame is dynamic, attach the coordinate epoch and its binding scope, producing a coordinate metadata record.
inputs: coordinate reference identifier as a governed IRI or register authority, code and version
coordinate epoch where the frame is dynamic
preconditions: the coordinate reference resolves to a definition or to a governed snapshot
the frame dynamics classification for the reference is recorded
effects: the coordinate set becomes interpretable without out-of-band assumptions about frame or epoch
an unresolved reference or a missing epoch on a dynamic frame is recorded as incomplete rather than silently defaulted

functions.name: Validate epoch completeness and time-role separation
functions.description: Check that a dynamic reference carries a coordinate epoch at a declared scope, and that coordinate epoch, observation time, transformation reference epoch, definition publication time and ingestion time are held in distinct roles with correct notation.
outputs: list of violated rules with severity
preconditions: a coordinate reference binding exists for the coordinate set
the epoch policy in force is identified
effects: records a pass or fail state on this model's own record
blocks positional use flagged by policy while an epoch is unresolved
does not modify coordinates and does not perform any epoch propagation

functions.name: Resolve and pin a reference definition
functions.description: Resolve a coordinate reference against the cited register or a supplied definition, normalize it to a canonical form, and store it as a pinned snapshot with register authority, version, code and integrity digest. The register itself is read, never maintained.
inputs: register authority and version to resolve against
supplied definition text where the reference is non-register
preconditions: the register authority and version to resolve against are declared
read access to the register or to the supplied definition is available under its terms of use
effects: later register revisions cannot silently change how historic coordinates are interpreted
an unresolvable reference produces an unresolved record rather than an assumed definition
no register entry is created, amended or deprecated by this function

functions.name: Record a deformation model reference
functions.description: Record the identifier, publisher, version label and declared spatial and temporal extent of the deformation or point-motion model a consumer must apply, together with the out-of-extent disposition. No displacement is computed, interpolated or stored.
inputs: deformation model citation from the publishing authority
subject location and required epoch range
outputs: applicability outcome for the subject location and epoch range
preconditions: the frame is classified as dynamic or semi-dynamic, or the subject spans epochs
the publishing authority and version label of the cited model are known
effects: a consumer can locate the governing model and know whether it applies
evaluation, grid distribution and versioning of the model remain with its publishing authority
no displacement value is produced by this model

functions.name: Assess compound reference composition
functions.description: Enumerate the component references of a compound coordinate reference, verify the declared order and the independence condition, derive the resulting axis sequence with directions and units, and determine the epoch applicability scope.
inputs: compound reference identifier or component reference list
component definitions or their pinned snapshots
preconditions: each component reference resolves to a definition or a governed snapshot
the declared component sequence is present and not inferred from a code
effects: axis order and units become explicit rather than assumed
a composition failing the independence condition is rejected and recorded, not silently flattened
no coordinate values are reordered or converted by this function

functions.name: Classify and gate a non-register definition
functions.description: Decide whether an unknown, custom, engineering-local, deprecated or superseded reference is sufficiently defined for use, or must be held as unresolved, and route custom definitions to the approving role.
inputs: candidate reference as supplied by the producer
any accompanying definition payload or anchor description
outputs: definition sufficiency state with missing elements listed
custom reference definition package where sufficiency is met
preconditions: a register resolution attempt has been made and its outcome recorded
the approving role for custom definitions is identified
effects: a bare local name or numeric code is recorded as unresolved and blocks the uses named in policy
an approved custom definition becomes usable without external lookup
no default reference is substituted for an unresolved one

composition.purpose: WM-XCT-033 is the registered child of the parent geometry model. The parent owns geometry representation, topology, validity and spatial extent semantics; this entry contributes only the reference-frame, epoch and definition context that the parent's coordinates are expressed against. Geometry primitives and operations are not re-modelled here.

composition.target: Any adopting subject model whose records carry coordinates
composition.purpose: As a mixin, this entry is attached to subject models that hold positional data, contributing reference identification, frame dynamics, epoch binding and definition sufficiency context. It introduces no subject identity, no subject lifecycle and no subject-specific business rules.

composition.target: ISO 19111:2019 / OGC Abstract Specification Topic 2: Referencing by coordinates (18-005r5)
composition.purpose: Declared alignment of this entry's vocabulary to the ISO 19111 conceptual schema for dynamic reference frame, frame reference epoch, coordinate epoch, coordinate metadata, datum ensemble, point motion operation, compound, temporal, vertical and engineering CRS. Alignment is asserted at element level and is not a conformance claim; conformance would require the standard's own conformance-class evidence.

composition.target: OGC Well-known text representation of coordinate reference systems (ISO 19162:2019 / OGC 18-010 series)
composition.purpose: Encoding alignment for pinned definition snapshots and compound composition records. The WKT version used is recorded per snapshot because element sets differ between WKT-CRS 2.0.6 and 2.1. This entry does not define or extend the grammar.

composition.target: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset (IOGP Geomatics Committee register)
composition.purpose: Carry register authority, definition code, register version, canonical snapshot and digest as reference context. Entry creation, revision, deprecation, data-management policy and publication of the register remain wholly with IOGP; this entry never mirrors the register or acts as a second register.

composition.target: IERS ITRS realization series (ITRF) and national frame realizations
composition.purpose: Carry the realization identity, its defining authority and its frame reference epoch as a reference. Computation, adjustment, publication and post-seismic modelling of realizations remain with IERS and the national geodetic agencies.

composition.target: Deformation model publications (OGC Topic 24 functional model and national agency deformation products)
composition.purpose: Reference the governing deformation or point-motion model with its version and declared extent. Element decomposition, spatial and time function evaluation, grid interpolation, distribution and version release stay with the publishing authority and with the coordinate-operation model that executes them.

Record the transformation reference epoch and the citation of an applicable coordinate operation or point motion operation. Operation selection, parameterization, pipeline construction, execution, accuracy assessment and the audit trail of executed transformations belong entirely to that model.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension temporal and calendar model
composition.purpose: Compose time-scale realization, leap-second tables and calendar arithmetic from the Dimension's temporal model. This entry records only which time scale a temporal axis realizes and the temporal datum origin; it neither realizes nor converts between time scales.

composition.target: Adopting Dimension retention, access and disposition policy
composition.purpose: Reference the policy that owns retention periods, legal holds, erasure decisions and their execution for records that cite this entry's definitions. This entry records disposition state and the owning policy reference only, and does not execute or audit disposal.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate a geodetic reference owner accountable for which registers, frame realizations, datum ensembles and deformation-model references are admissible for its subjects.
The owner package must pin a default register authority and register version, and publish the rule under which non-register definitions are accepted, amended or refused.
The owner package must state the positional tolerance that decides whether datum-ensemble referencing is admissible in place of a named realization.
The owner package must name which external model or system owns transformation execution, deformation evaluation and register maintenance, since this entry owns none of them.
The owner package must state the epoch policy: whether a dynamic reference without a coordinate epoch is refused, quarantined or accepted with a recorded unresolved state.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use the governed coordinate reference IRI as the primary reference form, following the pattern http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/{authority}/{version}/{code} where the authority publishes one. Locally minted identifiers for custom or engineering definitions live in the adopting Dimension's own namespace, must be visibly distinguishable from register codes, and must never reuse or shadow a register authority code. Deformation-model and geoid-model references use the publishing authority's own identifier namespace unchanged.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-033 record in the Vercy world-model registry, with parent WM-XCT-010
EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset as pinned register authority and version
OGC Naming Authority coordinate reference definition IRIs
National geodetic agency realization and deformation-model publication series cited per subject region

canonicalization_rules: The canonical definition form is a single normalized WKT-CRS string or an equivalent PROJJSON object at a named schema version; whitespace, keyword case and numeric formatting are normalized before any digest is computed, and the WKT or schema version used is recorded with the snapshot.

Epochs are stored in both the decimal-year form used by geodetic sources and an RFC 3339 instant with seconds and an explicit offset; the decimal-year form is authoritative for geodetic arithmetic and the RFC 3339 form is authoritative for record-level comparison.

Compound components are canonically ordered by their explicit sequence index, and the resulting axis order with direction and unit is recorded explicitly; axis order is never inferred from a coordinate reference code or name.

Frame dynamics, temporal axis kind, vertical axis direction and non-register kind are stored as controlled codes with the citing clause or register attribute, never as free text inferred from a definition name.
patch_rules: A change to a coordinate reference identifier, coordinate epoch, register version pin, compound component set or component order creates a new record version; these fields are never edited in place.

Every patch must declare whether it changes the interpretation of already-published coordinates; interpretation-changing patches require the geodetic reference owner's approval before they take effect.
Superseding a pinned definition snapshot never deletes the prior snapshot: the prior snapshot is marked superseded, retains its digest, and remains resolvable for coordinates that cite it.

Upstream register deprecation is recorded as an observed supersession event with its own observation timestamp, distinct from the register's publication date, and never as a local edit to the pinned definition text.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional coordinate epoch, deformation-model reference, vertical component or alignment statement is backward compatible. Changing frame dynamics classification, register version pin, axis order or an epoch value is breaking and requires a new record version.

A consumer that cannot carry a coordinate epoch must reject a dynamic reference or record an explicit degradation decision; silently dropping the epoch is prohibited because coordinates in a dynamic reference are ambiguous without it.
Alignments to external vocabularies are declared per element; where no alignment target exists the absence is recorded as a gap rather than approximated to the nearest term.
A pinned snapshot expressed under one WKT or schema version is not silently re-serialized to another; re-expression creates a new snapshot in the sequence with its own digest.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the register authority's own code for the definition together with the register version (for example a geodetic parameter register code plus its dataset release), or the originating master system's identifier for the coordinate set that a coordinate metadata record annotates.

Governed global identifier or IRI: the authority-published coordinate reference IRI including its version segment, or the publishing authority's own identifier for a deformation model, geoid model or frame realization.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither an authoritative master-system identifier nor a governed IRI exists, as for a purely local engineering definition.

Never an identifier: a coordinate epoch, a frame reference epoch, a register release date, a definition publication date, a deformation-model version label that happens to look like a date, or any other date-like value.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All record timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time and observation or ingestion time are recorded separately whenever they differ: definition publication time and observation time are event times attributable to an external authority or a survey, while ingestion time is this model's own record time, and none of them may be substituted for another. Coordinate epoch and frame reference epoch are geodetic reference instants, not record timestamps: they are stored in decimal-year form together with an RFC 3339 equivalent carrying seconds and an offset, and must never be read as, or written from, record creation, observation or ingestion time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts, principally pinned definition snapshots, are named by a stable subject key (register authority plus definition code, or the governed IRI) followed by a monotonically increasing sequence number, with the captured register version carried as an attribute. The sequence number is never a date and is never derived from a publisher's date-styled version label; where a publisher names its releases by approximate publication date, that label is stored verbatim as a version attribute only.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored definition text carries a digest computed over its canonical form together with the register authority, register version and definition code. Verification recomputes the digest from the canonical form; a snapshot whose digest does not reproduce is marked unverified, is excluded from interpreting coordinates, and is escalated to the reference definition steward with the failing digest recorded.

policies: No coordinate set referenced to a dynamic frame is accepted without a coordinate epoch, or without an explicit, approved unresolved-epoch record naming the uses it blocks; no default epoch is ever substituted.

A non-register reference is accepted only with a resolvable definition or a complete governed snapshot. A bare local name, a project label or a numeric code without register authority and version is recorded as unresolved and blocks positional use.

This entry records references, definitions and applicability context only. It does not execute transformations, evaluate deformation models, realize time scales, maintain registers, or hold audit trails for any of those activities; each is routed to the model or authority named in the composition links.
Register content is never mirrored wholesale. Only definitions actually cited by subject records are pinned, and redistribution of pinned text follows the register authority's terms of use.
Axis order, axis direction and units are always recorded explicitly with the reference; they are never inferred from a code, a name or a carrier convention.

read: Read a coordinate reference binding, its epochs, its binding scope and its resolved definition by subject key, by governed IRI, or by register authority, code and version.
Read the cited deformation-model reference, its version label and its declared extent, together with the applicability outcome, without triggering any evaluation.
Read pinned definition snapshots by sequence position and by captured register version, including superseded snapshots, so historic coordinates stay interpretable.
Read unresolved-state and out-of-extent records so a consumer can see precisely which uses are blocked and why.
create: Create a coordinate metadata record binding a coordinate set to a coordinate reference and, where the frame is dynamic, to a coordinate epoch at a declared binding scope.
Create a pinned definition snapshot capturing register authority, register version, definition code, canonical text and integrity digest.
Create a compound reference composition record with explicit component sequence, resulting axis order and independence assessment outcome.
Create a custom reference definition package only after the sufficiency assessment passes and the approving role has recorded approval.
update: Update by creating a new record version: frame dynamics classification, register version pin, coordinate epoch, compound component set and component order are versioned rather than edited in place.
Update supersession state when an upstream register deprecation or replacement is observed, recording the observation timestamp separately from the register's own publication date.
Update sufficiency state when a previously unresolved reference becomes resolvable, retaining the prior unresolved record and the reason it was raised.
Update verification outcome and last-verified timestamp on a pinned snapshot without altering its canonical text or digest.
delete: Records of this model are not hard-deleted while any coordinate set still cites them. Removal is by tombstone that preserves register authority, definition code, register version, digest, supersession state and the reason for disposal, so that historic coordinates remain interpretable rather than becoming silently ambiguous.

The retention minimum for a pinned definition snapshot, a coordinate metadata record and a compound composition record is the retention period of the coordinates that cite them; disposition is deferred until the last citing coordinate set has itself been disposed of.

Execution of deletion, erasure, legal hold and final disposition is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention, access and disposition policy together with the master system that holds the coordinate set. This model neither executes nor audits those actions; it records only the disposition state, the effective date and a reference to the owning policy.

Register entries, frame realization publications, deformation-model grids and geoid models are never deleted by this model. Upstream deprecation or withdrawal is recorded as supersession state on the local snapshot; removal from the upstream register is solely the register authority's action.

Custom definition packages that disclose a restricted site anchor follow the access exception on disposal: the anchor payload may be redacted on schedule while the tombstone, digest and identifier are retained.

roles.name: Geodetic reference owner
responsibilities: Approve the admissible registers, frame realizations and register version pins for the Dimension.
Decide whether datum-ensemble referencing meets the subject's stated positional tolerance.
Approve interpretation-changing patches and static-treatment decisions for dynamic frames.

roles.name: Reference definition steward
responsibilities: Resolve, normalize, pin and verify definition snapshots and their integrity digests.
Record upstream deprecation and supersession with a separate observation timestamp.
Maintain element-level alignment statements to external vocabularies without asserting conformance.

roles.name: Coordinate metadata author
responsibilities: Bind coordinate sets to references, coordinate epochs and binding scope.
Record observation time, coordinate epoch, transformation reference epoch, publication time and ingestion time in distinct roles.
Raise unresolved-epoch and unresolved-definition records instead of substituting defaults.

roles.name: Interoperability reviewer
responsibilities: Assess whether a target carrier can convey epoch, compound components and axis order, and record the degradation or rejection decision.
Record conflicts where a standard, carrier or implementation cannot express required context.
Review round-trip behaviour when the epoch binding scope differs between producer and consumer.

roles.name: Dimension data custodian
responsibilities: Apply the Dimension's retention, tombstone and access rules to this model's records.
Route deletion and erasure execution to the owning policy and the master system holding the coordinates.
Enforce register terms of use when pinned definition text is shared outside the Dimension.

access.default_rule: Coordinate reference identifiers, frame dynamics, epochs, alignment statements and unresolved-state records are readable by any agent authorized to read the subject's coordinates. Write access to bindings, snapshots and composition records is restricted to the reference definition steward and the coordinate metadata author, and approval of custom definitions and interpretation-changing patches is restricted to the geodetic reference owner.
exceptions: A custom or engineering definition whose anchor discloses a restricted or sensitive site location is readable only by roles cleared for that site's location data; the reference identifier and sufficiency state remain visible while the anchor payload is withheld.

Definition text pinned from a register that restricts redistribution is shared outside the Dimension only as register authority, code, register version and digest; the canonical text is withheld and the withholding reason is recorded.
Unresolved-state, out-of-extent and unverified-digest records are always readable to consumers of the affected coordinates, because concealing them would allow silent misinterpretation.
Where a subject's coordinates are themselves access-restricted, the coordinate metadata record inherits that restriction; the reference definition it cites does not.
audit_requirements: Every change to a register version pin, frame dynamics classification, compound component order, coordinate epoch or supersession state records the acting role, the reason and an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and an explicit offset in this model's own change log.
Every digest verification records its outcome, the algorithm used and the verification timestamp against the snapshot it verified.

This model's change log covers only its own records. Audit trails for transformation execution, deformation evaluation, register maintenance and downstream use of coordinates are owned by the referenced operational models and authorities and are neither duplicated nor asserted here.

required_fields: Pinned register authority and register version
Epoch policy: whether a dynamic reference without a coordinate epoch is refused, quarantined or recorded as unresolved
Named owners for transformation execution, deformation evaluation and retention execution
read_order: AGENTS.md — identity, type and the four resource URLs, plus the pinned register authority and epoch policy
Specification URL — model scope, out-of-scope list, boundary notes and composition links, read before any record is created
Storage type URL — record and artefact shapes, canonical forms, digest rules and the exclusive artefact rule
Interface URL — read and write operations, access scopes and the access exceptions
Processes URL — binding, epoch validation, definition resolution and pinning, supersession observation and disposition-state processes

coverage.claim: This structure covers the dynamic, temporal, compound and non-register coordinate-reference context an agent needs to interpret, validate and operate positional data: frame dynamics and frame reference epoch, coordinate epoch and its binding scope, strict separation of epoch from record time, datum realization versus ensemble, deformation-model references and their applicability, temporal and vertical components, compound composition and ordering, non-register definition sufficiency and pinned register provenance. It is grounded in ISO 19111 / OGC Topic 2, OGC WKT-CRS, OGC Topic 24, OGC API - Features Part 2, the EPSG register, IERS ITRF and two national geodetic agencies, with implementation evidence from PROJ and GDAL. It does not claim completeness for geometry representation, register maintenance, deformation computation, transformation execution or time-scale realization, all of which are explicitly external.

checklist.notes: Register authority plus code plus register version is the authoritative master-system identifier; the governed CRS IRI is second; a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID is last. Coordinate epochs, frame reference epochs, release dates and date-styled version labels are explicitly excluded as identifiers, and locally minted identifiers must not shadow register codes.

Definition supersession and deprecation state, unresolved and out-of-extent states, verification outcome, and serial snapshot versioning. The upstream register's own entry lifecycle is observed and recorded, never owned; deprecation upstream produces a local supersession record rather than an edit.

Ensemble-to-member, compound-to-component, reference-to-realization, reference-to-deformation-model and reference-to-geoid-model links are all modelled as typed references with a declared external owner, and epoch applicability across compound components is explicit.

Frame reference epoch, coordinate epoch, observation time, transformation reference epoch, definition publication time and ingestion time are five distinct data elements with a time role map and a dedicated validation function. Temporal CRS origin, axis kind, unit, calendar and realized time scale are separately recorded.

Register authority and version, defining authority and document version, deformation-model publisher and version label, geoid model version, canonical form identifier and digest over the definition text, plus separate observation timestamps for upstream changes.

Five roles with disjoint responsibilities; register maintenance, deformation evaluation, transformation execution, time-scale realization and retention execution are each assigned to a named external owner in boundary notes and composition links.

Epoch completeness and time-role separation, compound independence and order, non-register definition sufficiency, and digest verification. Every failure produces a recorded blocking state rather than a substituted default.

Default read follows the subject's coordinate access, write restricted to steward and author, approval restricted to the geodetic reference owner; exceptions cover restricted site anchors, register redistribution terms, and mandatory visibility of unresolved and unverified states.

Tombstone-and-retain tied to the life of the citing coordinates, with tombstone content specified. Execution of deletion, erasure and legal hold is explicitly owned by the Dimension's retention policy and the coordinate master system; upstream register content is never deleted by this model.

Governed CRS IRIs, WKT-CRS and PROJJSON canonical forms with recorded version, carrier-specific epoch fields, an explicit degradation-or-rejection decision where a carrier cannot hold the context, and recorded conflicts where standards disagree.

Frame dynamics, temporal axis kind, vertical axis direction and non-register kind are declared controlled codes with a citing clause or register attribute; none may be inferred from a definition name or code.
Deformation-model spatial extent, temporal validity interval and frame extent are recorded as applicability context, with an explicit out-of-extent disposition and prohibited-use list.

Only published datum ensemble accuracy and declared model extents are recorded. Survey accuracy, error propagation, deformation-model uncertainty evaluation and fitness-for-purpose budgets are left to a measurement model and are not covered here; OGC Topic 24 defines model uncertainty attributes that this entry cites but does not consume.
No credentials, keys or trust material are held. The one sensitivity vector, an engineering anchor disclosing a restricted site, is handled as an access exception rather than as a security model.
Primitives, topology, validity, tessellation and spatial indexing belong to the parent geometry model WM-XCT-010; this entry supplies only the reference context those primitives are expressed in.

known_omissions: Parametric CRS and parametric datum are not developed as their own finding, although ISO 19111 admits spatio-parametric compound CRS; a parametric component would currently be carried only as a generic compound component.
Derived CRS and projected CRS conversion parameters, and map-projection method context, are captured only inside the pinned definition snapshot and are not decomposed into their own findings.
Bound CRS and the embedded hub-transformation pattern found in legacy definitions are not modelled; such definitions would be classified as non-register or superseded and pinned as text.
Non-Earth, planetary, inertial and orbital reference frames are outside the retrieved evidence base and are not covered by the frame dynamics classification as scoped.
Moving-platform engineering frames (vessel, vehicle, robot base) are admitted through the engineering-definition finding, but the kinematic chain and its own time semantics are not modelled here.
Sounding, tidal and chart datums are covered only generically under the vertical reference finding; hydrographic-specific practice was not researched to primary sources.
IOGP Guidance Note 25 and EPSG Guidance Note 7-7 on ETRS89 were identified at page level but their full texts were not retrieved, so European regional practice is cited by reference only.
conflicts: RFC 7946 fixes all GeoJSON coordinates to a WGS 84 geographic CRS and removed the crs member entirely, so a GeoJSON projection cannot carry a coordinate reference or a coordinate epoch at all. Conveying dynamic context therefore requires an out-of-band agreement or a different carrier, and this model records the loss as a degradation decision rather than assuming a carrier exists.

OGC Topic 2 states that dataset metadata should include coordinate epoch information for a dynamic CRS, and OGC API - Features Part 2 makes storageCrsCoordinateEpoch a recommendation rather than a requirement. The stricter internal policy stated here (no dynamic reference without an epoch or an approved unresolved record) is therefore a governance choice of the adopting Dimension, not a conformance claim against either standard.

WKT-CRS 2.0.6 (OGC 18-010r7 / ISO 19162:2019) and WKT-CRS 2.1 (OGC 18-010r11, 2023) differ in their element sets, with the later revision adding elements such as anchor epoch and revised ensemble handling. A pinned snapshot must therefore record which WKT version it is expressed in, and re-serialization between versions is treated as a new snapshot.

Epoch binding scope differs between the conceptual model and implementations: ISO 19111 associates the coordinate epoch with a coordinate set, whereas GDAL binds the epoch to the CRS at dataset or layer level and states that almost no format allows per-observation epoch storage. Per-observation epochs may therefore not survive a round trip, which is why binding scope is a required declared element.

A bare register code without a register version can change meaning over time, because the EPSG Dataset advances through versioned releases and entries may be deprecated. Citing a code alone is a widespread practice that this model treats as insufficient provenance.

CGPM Resolution 4 (2022) decided that the maximum UT1-UTC difference will be increased in or before 2035, with an implementation plan due at the 28th CGPM. Leap-second behaviour on UTC-based temporal axes may therefore change within the retention life of stored records, so leap-second exposure is recorded as a declared constraint with a review trigger.

Frame naming is not a reliable indicator of dynamics: several widely used reference names denote ensembles or have both static and dynamic realizations, so the model refuses to infer frame dynamics from a name or code and requires an explicit classification with a citing clause.
regional_assumptions: North America: NOAA NGS plans four plate-fixed dynamic terrestrial reference frames (NATRF2022, PATRF2022, CATRF2022, MATRF2022) each defined relative to ITRF2020, plus a gravity-based geopotential datum realized through an updated geoid model. The published implementation timeline was not independently confirmed here, so these frame names are recorded as references rather than as effective defaults.

New Zealand: NZGD2000 is a semi-dynamic datum aligned to ITRF96 at epoch 2000.0, with a versioned deformation model comprising a secular velocity component and earthquake patches. Its versions are named by approximate publication date (for example 20180701), a convention this model stores verbatim as a version label and explicitly refuses to treat as an identifier or a coordinate epoch.

Australia: a two-frame approach pairs a static plate-fixed datum with a time-dependent frame, with a plate motion model used to propagate between epochs. This was observed only through secondary summaries because the primary national committee pages redirected or timed out during research, so it is held as an unverified regional note rather than a grounded structural claim.

Europe: ETRS89 practice is addressed by an EPSG guidance note identified but not retrieved. Plate-fixed European practice is assumed to follow the same plate-fixed pattern as the North American and Australian cases and is flagged as unverified.

Global versus regional realization: ITRF2020 has reference epoch 2015.0 while national frames adopt their own reference epochs, so a coordinate epoch is meaningful only together with the frame it qualifies; cross-region merging without both is treated as unsafe.

Extraterrestrial and planetary bodies, and marine or airborne moving-platform frames, are outside the researched evidence base; regional assumptions here concern terrestrial Earth-referenced practice only.
adversarial_checks: Checked every finding and function against the relation rationales for target ownership: no node evaluates a deformation model, interpolates a grid, executes a transformation, realizes a time scale or maintains a register. The deformation finding is deliberately inline-only precisely so that no local artefact implies custody of a grid or of a displacement computation.

Checked that audit-trail semantics are scoped to this model's own change log, with an explicit disclaimer that audit trails for transformation execution, deformation evaluation, register maintenance and downstream coordinate use belong to the referenced operational models.

Attacked the confusion this model exists to prevent: verified that no data element defines a coordinate epoch as a record timestamp, that five time roles are separately typed, that a time role map is mandatory, and that a dedicated validation question and function guard the substitution in both directions.

Tested the 'a code is enough' counterexample: an EPSG code without register version, a local grid name and an undefined srs row are each explicitly declared insufficient and routed to an unresolved state with a prohibited-use list, rather than resolved by a default.

Tested whether frame dynamics could be inferred from a CRS name or code and concluded it cannot, so frame dynamics is a mandatory declared code carrying the citing clause or register attribute; the same reasoning removed any inference of axis order from a code.

Tested the interoperability floor against RFC 7946 GeoJSON, which can carry neither a CRS reference nor an epoch, confirming that carrier incapacity must be recorded as a conflict and a degradation decision instead of being silently absorbed.

Checked that the delete rules cannot orphan historic coordinates: tombstones retain register authority, code, version, digest and supersession state, retention is tied to the life of citing coordinates, and execution is assigned to an external policy owner rather than claimed here.

Checked artefact discipline: four findings declare artefacts with a null rationale and six declare an empty artefact array with a substantive rationale; no finding populates both, and each inline rationale names the external owner of the document that would otherwise be duplicated.
